I'll start with a read-only look at the repo so I can suggest specific cleanups instead of guessing. I won't change anything yet.

TOOL: git status --short && git log --oneline -n 10 && ls -la

Once I see the output, I'll group what I find into candidate cleanups, such as untracked junk files, stale build artifacts, unused code, or formatting and lint issues. Each one will be listed separately so you can choose which to apply. That keeps the diff limited to what you actually want changed.

It would also help to know what "clean up" means to you. Are you after tidying the tree (stray files, ignored artifacts), code-level cleanup (dead code, unused imports, lint), docs, or dependencies? Any of those is a different job, and a targeted pass is easier to review than a sweeping one.
